This line is incorrect and should be fixed:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/65d14909ee3678b942ed87308a55cad576119ea9/homeassistant/components/honeywell/__init__.py#L127

We should just await the coroutine function `_retry`. It should not run on the executor.

> The changes are going in the wrong direction. The long term fix is probably to use our update coordinator.
> 
> https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data#coordinated-single-api-poll-for-data-for-all-entities
> 
> For now just set parallell updates and increase the minimum time between updates if needed. And fix the retry call to await the coroutine function.

The reason I decided against going with the Data Update Coordinator was because of this statement in the document you linked:

> This API will have a single method to fetch data for all the entities that you have in Home Assistant.

The TCC API does not work like this. It has separate endpoints for each climate device. Should I still use the Data Update Coordinator?

Ultimately, I believe the entities were all updating themselves as a multiple of how many climate entities the user has in TCC. This is what I am trying to fix.

Currently we have the Throttle on the data update method which fetches data for all devices. Even though all entities call the data update method only the first call within the minimum update interval will go through the throttle.

Currently we also update all devices in one go in the throttled update method. So using the data update coordinator won't make this worse. We could also implement one coordinator per device if we want to differentiate the API calls between the devices. The coordinator has the advantage that it won't fetch data on an interval unless there's a connected listener (entity). So if the user disables all entities supported by a coordinator, the coordinator will stop the scheduled API calls.

What are the API call limits of the Honeywell service? To choose the best approach we need to understand what limits the API has in place, and how these are spread across devices and users etc.

>

Hard to say what the limits are for TCC. I don't see any documentation anywhere. I am going to contact honeywell to see if I can get API developer authorization.

In the mean time, I can revert the most recent commit. But we still need to throttle the loop somehow. Also some users with a single thermostat are experiencing the rate limiting issue (though this may be unrelated).

Do you know of a way for us to delay iterations in the loop by maybe 10 seconds?

Just a thought for a future patch, but would it be possible to detect the rate limiting error, suspend for 5 minutes (or a user defined time period), reauthenticate, and resume polling with the new auth token?
Why should we reauthenticate unless the authentication fails? That's an extra burden on the user. We should just make sure we don't get rate limited.
